1) the use of PET/CT is associated with a significant increase in the detection rate of lung cancer, 2) it is associated with an increase in the detection of early stage disease, 3) PET/CT is a cost-effective strategy in the diagnosis of lung cancer, and 4) the use of the PET/CT is cost effective in the diagnosis of early stage lung cancer.
The use of PET-CT for staging of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is cost-effective compared with conventional imaging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the value of (18) F-FDG PET/CT for early diagnosis of lung carcinoma.
the early diagnosis of lung carcinoma by (18)F-FDG PET/CT and the value of (18)FDG PET/CT in the diagnosis of lung carcinoma.

the application of (18)fluorodeoxygluce positron emission tomograpy (18FDG-PET) in early diagnosis of primary lung cancer, and its value in differential diagnosis of benign and malignant lung nodules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PET/CT is an effective and reliable method in the early diagnosis of lung carcinoma.
the value of (18)FDG PET/CT is high and the sensitivity is high for the diagnosis of lung cancer, especially for peripheral lung cancer and small-sized lung cancer.
FDG PET/CT is a valuable tool for early diagnosis and staging of lung cancer, but its role in the follow-up after treatment is limited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (18)F-FDG PET/CT is a valuable diagnostic method in early diagnosis of primary lung cancer and the early detection of metastasis.
(18)F-FDG PET/CT is a useful method in early detection and diagnosis of lung cancer, especially for early stage lung cancer.
(18)F-FDG PET/CT is the best noninvasive modality for the early detection of lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 18F-FDG-PET/CT scan has an important role in the early diagnosis of lung cancers.
the 18F-fluorine-2-deoxy-D-glucose positron emission/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) scan can be used to identify lung cancer at an early stage.
the combination of PET and CT scans can provide a better diagnosis of lung cancer than either scan can alone.
